rv.q: Relentlessly funny and endearingly emotional, it is a play for anyone who’s been scared of an uncertain future—that is to say, everyone.
Matt Schutz’s enjoyable comedy certainly checks all these boxes with this delightful 100-minute one-act.
Windows offers an uplifting reminder of new possibilities.

But it is also frustratingly unformed, with characters that aren’t quite there yet, and a plot that too frequently takes convenient shortcuts—thanks to a talk with a magical delivery woman, Olivia’s attitude changes just in time for the final scene.
For a world premiere, Windows is an intriguing beginning.

cn.t: Critics find this world premiere an engaging voyeuristic drama elevated by its appealing young cast, though some feel the production needs more polish. The Rear Window-inspired premise mostly works despite familiar elements.
